To find ${f}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}+y}) \\  & =2x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+y}) \\  & =2x\cdot (-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+y}) \\  & =(-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}})\cdot 2x \\  & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y)+{f}_{yx}(x,y) & =-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{4x}{({x}^{2}+y)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{e}^{2x-y}) \\  & =4{e}^{2x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-{e}^{2x-y}) \\  & ={e}^{2x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(0,1) & =4{e}^{2(0)-1}=4{e}^{-1} \\ {g}_{yy}(0,1) & ={e}^{2(0)-1}={e}^{-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(0,1)\cdot {g}_{yy}(0,1)=4{e}^{-1}\cdot {e}^{-1}=4{e}^{-2}.
$$

First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}) \\  & =6{x}^{2}y{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(6{x}^{2}y{z}^{2}) \\  & =12{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-1,2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(-1,2,1) & =12(-1)^{2}(2)(1)=24\end{aligned}
$$
